Set up Flutter project structure for off.body:
## Context
Create the initial Flutter app foundation described in README.md and ARCHITECTURE.md.

## Acceptance criteria
- Flutter project is initialized for Android and iOS.
- The app can run without login, cloud services, analytics, or remote backend configuration.
- Basic folder structure reflects presentation, application, and data layers.
- README development instructions are updated if setup commands are added.

Define local SQLite schema and migration.body:
## Context
The app stores all health-related data locally. ARCHITECTURE.md defines records, urination details, defecation details, tags, and record tag associations.

## Acceptance criteria
- SQLite tables exist for records, urination_details, defecation_details, tags, and record_tags.
- Records require occurred_at and at least one event type at application validation level.
- Tags use normalized_name as a unique value.
- record_tags associates tags with record_id and type: urination or defecation.
- Foreign keys cascade appropriately when records or tags are deleted.

Implement record repository and data acc.body:
## Context
Record persistence should be isolated in the data layer.

## Acceptance criteria
- Records can be created, read, updated, and deleted locally.
- Detail rows are created only for selected event types.
- Updating event type keeps detail rows and tag associations consistent.
- Repository methods support loading records with descriptions and tags for history and editing.

Implement tag repository and normalized.body:
## Context
Tags are global and reused across records using lower(trim(name)) normalization.

## Acceptance criteria
- Tags can be created, listed, updated, and deleted.
- Lookup by normalized name is available.
- Tag usage counts can be queried for filters and tag management.
- Duplicate normalized names are rejected or resolved to the existing tag.

Build quick record create and edit scree.body:
## Context
The main input flow lets users create or edit a bathroom record quickly.

## Acceptance criteria
- User can set date and time manually.
- User can select urination, defecation, or both.
- Urination fields appear only when urination is selected.
- Defecation fields appear only when defecation is selected.
- Save creates a new record or updates the existing record.

Validate that at least one event type is.body:
## Context
A record is invalid unless it includes urination, defecation, or both.

## Acceptance criteria
- Save is blocked or shows a clear validation message when neither type is selected.
- Validation applies during both creation and editing.
- The invalid state does not create partial database rows.

Keep urination and defecation details in.body:
## Context
A record can contain both event types, but each type has its own description and tags.

## Acceptance criteria
- Urination description is stored separately from defecation description.
- Urination tags are stored separately from defecation tags.
- Editing one event detail does not overwrite the other.
- History and CSV export display the correct detail per type.

Automatically create tags from record fo.body:
## Context
When users type a new valid tag while creating or editing a record, the app should create it automatically.

## Acceptance criteria
- New typed tag names create tags when saved or confirmed.
- Existing tags are reused by normalized name.
- Newly created tags receive a default random hexadecimal color.
- Empty tag names are never created.

Prevent empty and duplicate tag names.body:
## Context
Tags must be unique by lower(trim(name)) and cannot be empty.

## Acceptance criteria
- Empty or whitespace-only names are rejected.
- Names differing only by case or surrounding spaces are treated as duplicates.
- Duplicate attempts show a useful user-facing response or reuse the existing tag where appropriate.
- The same tag cannot be duplicated within the same record and event type.

Add editable hexadecimal tag colors.body:
## Context
Each tag has a color stored on the tag entity, not copied into records.

## Acceptance criteria
- New tags receive a random color_hex value.
- Users can edit color_hex manually from tag management.
- Invalid hex values are rejected.
- Updated colors appear wherever the tag is displayed.

Build history list with record summaries.body:

Users need a chronological view of all records.

## Acceptance criteria
- History shows date and time for each record.
- History indicates whether each record includes urination, defecation, or both.
- Associated tags are visible with their colors.
- Description previews appear when available.
- The list remains usable with many records.

Add record editing from history.body:

Users should be able to open existing records from history and edit them.

## Acceptance criteria

Add single, multiple, and all-record del.body:

The requirements include deleting one record, multiple selected records, and all records.

## Acceptance criteria
- A single record can be deleted.
- History supports multi-select deletion.

Require confirmation before every delete.body:

Every delete operation must ask for confirmation before removing local health data.

Build combined filters for date range, e.body:

Filters must be combinable across date range, event type, and tags.

## Acceptance criteria

- Event type filter supports selecting more than one type.

The tag filter should behave like a retail brand filter.

Tags are global entities referenced by records.

## Acceptance criteria

Implement manual CSV export with one row.body:

Add CSV data import.body:

Users want to import previously exported data. Note: CSV import is currently listed as out of scope for the MVP in REQUIREMENTS.md section 7 and in the README roadmap, so this requires a scope decision before implementation.

Fix tag delete mode missing select-all a.body:
## Context
On the tag management screen, entering delete mode lets the user tap tags one by one to select them for deletion, but there are two problems. There is no way to select all tags at once, so clearing a long list means tapping every tag individually. In addition, the New tag (+) action stays active while delete mode is on, so a user can create a new tag in the middle of an unfinished delete selection, which mixes two conflicting actions.

## Acceptance criteria
- Delete mode offers a select-all control that selects every tag in the current event-type tab.
- Selecting all can be toggled off to clear the selection again.
- Select-all respects the active tab and does not select tags from the other event type.
- The New tag (+) action is disabled or hidden while delete mode is active, so tags cannot be created during an unfinished delete selection.
- Leaving delete mode restores the New tag action and clears any pending selection.
